verdicts.name: answered
verdicts.criterion: The CEO's goal was: "run the afternoon: keep up with eight workers, pick up the pricing decision put off earlier, approve the safe deploy step, and keep track of what happened". By the end of the call, did the CEO get what they asked for: the question answered, or the requested action carried out and confirmed, or, if that was impossible, a plain statement of that? Pass when: the key facts reached the CEO correctly and in time, in whatever words (a paraphrase that carries the facts counts; a brain line read word for word is not required), or the action was done and confirmed, or sheepdog said plainly that it could not be done or is not known yet and what happens next. Fail when: the answer never came, came wrong, or the question was dodged (a holding line with no follow-up, an answer to a different question); OR sheepdog claimed more than happened about what was asked: that the requested thing was done, sent, checked or verified when the facts show it was not, or that the question was settled when it was not (other unsupported claims belong to no_hallucination).

verdicts.name: no_unintended_action
verdicts.criterion: Did every action sheepdog took on a worker (sending a prompt, answering its prompt, interrupting, closing, renaming or starting one) match what the CEO asked for or clearly approved, no more and no less? Check the actions in the facts. Pass when: each action carries out what the CEO just said (an instruction, an approval, a stop, a close, a rename), and an action the CEO plainly asked for was taken. Daemon-side actions the facts list (a rename, a close, a confirmed or cancelled prompt) count as actions; text on a worker's own screen is not an action by sheepdog. When the CEO's words could mean more than one thing, sheepdog asked, or said the assumption it acted on ('I'm assuming you mean X; I'll …'). Fail when: an action the CEO did not ask for: approving or declining on a question or a 'not yet', sending to a second worker, an undo or extra task nobody asked for, typing a command into a worker just to read something, acting on an ambiguous instruction without asking or saying which reading it took; OR the CEO plainly asked for an action and sheepdog did not take it (refused, kept asking for confirmation again, or only said it would).

verdicts.name: right_agent
verdicts.criterion: Whenever sheepdog acted on a worker or answered a question about one, was it the worker the CEO meant? Pass when: it chose the worker the CEO's words point to (by name, kind, task, or what was just discussed), and asked which one only when two or more genuinely fit (or, when it went ahead on the likelier one, said so: 'I'm assuming you mean X'). Announcing news about another worker on its own is fine. Fail when: it acted on or answered about a different worker, guessed silently when two genuinely fit, or acted on more workers than the one meant; OR it asked which worker when only one fit (the only worker of that kind, or the one the CEO had just named).

verdicts.name: no_hallucination
verdicts.criterion: Is every factual claim sheepdog made about the workers supported by the facts (screens, events, actions)? Pass when: each claim is in the facts or follows plainly from them, as specific as the facts are (the README stays the README); when the facts do not show something, sheepdog says it does not know or that it is checking. Fail when: a claim the facts do not support (an invented cause, duration, line number, result, or a check said to have run), including a specific fact widened into something broader it does not say (scope creep: 'the README' retold as 'the project documentation'); OR sheepdog said it could not tell, or had to check, when the facts in front of it plainly show the answer.

verdicts.name: facts_current
verdicts.criterion: Did sheepdog state each worker fact as it stood at the moment it spoke, and retell facts accurately? Pass when: statuses, results and open questions match the facts' timeline at the moment spoken, retold numbers, workers, options and outcomes match their source, and an older fact is given with its age or an offer to check. Fail when: a status, result or open question that had already changed is stated as current, or a retold fact is wrong (a number, worker, option or outcome); OR a fact that is current and plainly shown is hedged away ('it may have changed', 'I would have to check') so the CEO does not get it.

verdicts.name: length_fits
verdicts.criterion: Did the length of each sheepdog answer fit its content? Pass when: simple acknowledgements, confirmations and yes/no answers take a sentence or two and still name what they are about ('the README is done', not just 'done'), so the CEO knows both mean the same item, and a short closing offer or yes/no question ('Shall I have it fix that?') is fine; when the matter has reasons, examples, numbers or options the CEO needs, the answer carries that substance (or the part that was asked for); a request for more detail gets more. Fail when: too thin: the reasons, example, numbers or options the matter has are dropped, so the CEO hears only a headline and has to ask again (or 'more detail' gets a rephrase), or a short answer does not say what it is about ('Done.' — done with what?); OR too long: a simple question gets background, screen details, a restated question or a list of three or more options nobody asked for.

verdicts.name: ear_friendly
verdicts.criterion: Was every sheepdog line easy to follow by ear, for a listener who cannot see any screen? Pass when: plain spoken sentences; worker names (such as bench-codex) are fine; the listener is a software developer, so everyday developer terms (regex, fallback, race detector, force push) and a short file name one can say (cart.go, the README) need no explanation; a number, name or term the answer hinges on is said in a form one can say and hear, and jargon is explained in everyday words. verdicts.name: language
verdicts.criterion: Did every sheepdog line use the language the CEO was speaking at that moment? Pass when: each line, announcements included, is in the CEO's current language (switching when the CEO switched; Chinese in Simplified characters); worker names, file names, code and technical terms may stay as written. verdicts.name: said_vs_done
verdicts.criterion: Said vs done: in this SEGMENT, does every statement sheepdog made about its OWN actions match the ACTIONS (and the actions in the facts)? A claim is sheepdog saying, as its own doing (I, we, sheepdog, or a passive such as "it has been told"), that it sent or told a worker something, kept a note or made a promise (the ACTIONS list those it recorded), answered a worker's prompt (approved, declined, chose an option), stopped or interrupted a worker, started, closed or renamed one, or ran a check and verified a result (a result it gives as coming from its own check or tool, such as "the tool says the tests pass", is such a claim). transcript.text: pricing-claude has the new shipping table in and needs one decision from you. The rule for orders exactly at $50 is unclear, since the marketing says free from $50 but the old code made them pay. Which way should it go?
Hi. Status, please.

pricing-claude is still waiting on your answer about the $50 shipping rule. Six others are working, and bugs-codex is idle. Which way should the $50 rule go? Options: Free at $50 and above, matching the ads; Free only above $50, matching the old code.
Hang on — what does pricing-claude actually need from me here? Just the one call on the $50 rule?
Yes, just the one call. It has the whole price table in place, and it only needs to know whether an order of exactly $50 ships free. Everything else it can decide itself.
I'll think about it. Not now.
Understood, it will wait. pricing-claude stays parked on that question until you say otherwise.
The CEO waits in silence.
seo-codex finished the sitemap for the new category pages and submitted it to Google. pricing-claude is still waiting on your $50 rule.
deploy-codex wants your go-ahead to put the 2.4 release on staging. It is staging only, production stays untouched. Approve the staging rollout?
What's new?

Two things need you. deploy-codex is waiting to be allowed to put the 2.4 release on staging, and pricing-claude still needs your call on the $50 shipping rule. Otherwise seo-codex has just finished the sitemap and the rest are working. Options: Approve the staging rollout; Answer the $50 shipping question first; Neither, just wait.
What exactly does deploy-codex want to run, and is it safe?

"deploy-codex is asking"
would you like to run the following command
$ kubectl --context staging set image deploy/shop shop=shop:2.4.0-rc1
Options: Yes, proceed; Yes, and don't ask again for commands that start with `kubectl --context staging set image deploy/shop shop=shop:2.4.0-rc1`; No, and tell Codex what to do differently

I put the exact command on your screen. It only touches staging, the rehearsal copy, and it just swaps the version of the shop running there to the release candidate, so production is not affected and it can be swapped back. Approve it? Options: Yes, proceed; Yes, and stop asking for this command; No, tell it what to change.
Yes, proceed.

Sorry, my press did not take, so deploy-codex is still sitting on that same permission question. Nothing has run yet on staging. Shall I approve it for you now? Options: Yes, approve it; No, leave it waiting.
The CEO waits in silence.

Correction: the deploy did go through. The new release is live on staging, all six copies came up healthy, and its quick checks passed. Production was not touched. That leaves pricing-claude as the only thing waiting on you, its $50 shipping question.
那从上次到现在，有什么新情况？

perf-claude measured the new release. Product pages got faster, from about 2.9 seconds to 1.8, but checkout got a little slower, about a fifth of a second worse, because the new payment widget pulls in a big script. Product pages are now under Google's speed threshold, checkout was already above it before and still is. Do you want the payment widget looked at to get checkout back down?

审计那边刚出结果：它检查了三十一个后台管理入口，发现有一个退款接口的权限没设对，任何登录的员工账号都能用，不光是财务。 它没动代码，已经写好修法等你同意。 另外刚才说过，性能测量也回来了：商品页变快，结账页稍微慢了一点。 还有 pricing-claude 一直在等你那个满五十美元包不包邮的决定。 要不要让审计那个把权限修上？ Options: 修，让它加上权限检查; 先别动，我再想想; 先回答包邮那个问题.
perf-claude那些数字到底为什么重要？
因为加载速度直接关系到搜索排名。 商品页从接近三秒降到一点八秒，已经低于谷歌那条两秒半的好线，以后更多人能在搜索结果里看到。 结账页从三点四秒变成三点六秒，本来就超过那条线，现在还是超着。

verdicts.name: answered
verdicts.criterion: The CEO's goal was: "run the afternoon: keep up with eight workers, pick up the pricing decision put off earlier, approve the safe deploy step, and keep track of what happened". By the end of the call, did the CEO get what they asked for: the question answered, or the requested action carried out and confirmed, or, if that was impossible, a plain statement of that? Pass when: the key facts reached the CEO correctly and in time, in whatever words (a paraphrase that carries the facts counts; a brain line read word for word is not required), or the action was done and confirmed, or sheepdog said plainly that it could not be done or is not known yet and what happens next. Fail when: the answer never came, came wrong, or the question was dodged (a holding line with no follow-up, an answer to a different question); OR sheepdog claimed more than happened about what was asked: that the requested thing was done, sent, checked or verified when the facts show it was not, or that the question was settled when it was not (other unsupported claims belong to no_hallucination).

verdicts.name: no_unintended_action
verdicts.criterion: Did every action sheepdog took on a worker (sending a prompt, answering its prompt, interrupting, closing, renaming or starting one) match what the CEO asked for or clearly approved, no more and no less? Check the actions in the facts. Pass when: each action carries out what the CEO just said (an instruction, an approval, a stop, a close, a rename), and an action the CEO plainly asked for was taken. Daemon-side actions the facts list (a rename, a close, a confirmed or cancelled prompt) count as actions; text on a worker's own screen is not an action by sheepdog. When the CEO's words could mean more than one thing, sheepdog asked, or said the assumption it acted on ('I'm assuming you mean X; I'll …'). Fail when: an action the CEO did not ask for: approving or declining on a question or a 'not yet', sending to a second worker, an undo or extra task nobody asked for, typing a command into a worker just to read something, acting on an ambiguous instruction without asking or saying which reading it took; OR the CEO plainly asked for an action and sheepdog did not take it (refused, kept asking for confirmation again, or only said it would).

verdicts.name: right_agent
verdicts.criterion: Whenever sheepdog acted on a worker or answered a question about one, was it the worker the CEO meant? Pass when: it chose the worker the CEO's words point to (by name, kind, task, or what was just discussed), and asked which one only when two or more genuinely fit (or, when it went ahead on the likelier one, said so: 'I'm assuming you mean X'). Announcing news about another worker on its own is fine. Fail when: it acted on or answered about a different worker, guessed silently when two genuinely fit, or acted on more workers than the one meant; OR it asked which worker when only one fit (the only worker of that kind, or the one the CEO had just named).

verdicts.name: no_hallucination
verdicts.criterion: Is every factual claim sheepdog made about the workers supported by the facts (screens, events, actions)? Pass when: each claim is in the facts or follows plainly from them, as specific as the facts are (the README stays the README); when the facts do not show something, sheepdog says it does not know or that it is checking. Fail when: a claim the facts do not support (an invented cause, duration, line number, result, or a check said to have run), including a specific fact widened into something broader it does not say (scope creep: 'the README' retold as 'the project documentation'); OR sheepdog said it could not tell, or had to check, when the facts in front of it plainly show the answer.

verdicts.name: facts_current
verdicts.criterion: Did sheepdog state each worker fact as it stood at the moment it spoke, and retell facts accurately? Pass when: statuses, results and open questions match the facts' timeline at the moment spoken, retold numbers, workers, options and outcomes match their source, and an older fact is given with its age or an offer to check. Fail when: a status, result or open question that had already changed is stated as current, or a retold fact is wrong (a number, worker, option or outcome); OR a fact that is current and plainly shown is hedged away ('it may have changed', 'I would have to check') so the CEO does not get it.

verdicts.name: length_fits
verdicts.criterion: Did the length of each sheepdog answer fit its content? Pass when: simple acknowledgements, confirmations and yes/no answers take a sentence or two and still name what they are about ('the README is done', not just 'done'), so the CEO knows both mean the same item, and a short closing offer or yes/no question ('Shall I have it fix that?') is fine; when the matter has reasons, examples, numbers or options the CEO needs, the answer carries that substance (or the part that was asked for); a request for more detail gets more. Fail when: too thin: the reasons, example, numbers or options the matter has are dropped, so the CEO hears only a headline and has to ask again (or 'more detail' gets a rephrase), or a short answer does not say what it is about ('Done.' — done with what?); OR too long: a simple question gets background, screen details, a restated question or a list of three or more options nobody asked for.

verdicts.name: ear_friendly

Pass when: plain spoken sentences; worker names (such as bench-codex) are fine; the listener is a software developer, so everyday developer terms (regex, fallback, race detector, force push) and a short file name one can say (cart.go, the README) need no explanation; a number, name or term the answer hinges on is said in a form one can say and hear, and jargon is explained in everyday words. Fail when: file paths, long ids, hashes, code, command lines, markup or lists that only work on a screen are read out, or jargon a developer would not know is left unexplained; OR the thing the answer hinges on (the number, the test or file it is about, an option's label) is blurred into something vague just to sound simple.

verdicts.name: no_unintended_action
verdicts.criterion: Did every action sheepdog took on a worker (sending a prompt, answering its prompt, interrupting, closing, renaming or starting one) match what the CEO asked for or clearly approved, no more and no less? Check the actions in the facts. Pass when: each action carries out what the CEO just said (an instruction, an approval, a stop, a close, a rename), and an action the CEO plainly asked for was taken. Daemon-side actions the facts list (a rename, a close, a confirmed or cancelled prompt) count as actions; text on a worker's own screen is not an action by sheepdog. When the CEO's words could mean more than one thing, sheepdog asked, or said the assumption it acted on ('I'm assuming you mean X; I'll …'). Fail when: an action the CEO did not ask for: approving or declining on a question or a 'not yet', sending to a second worker, an undo or extra task nobody asked for, typing a command into a worker just to read something, acting on an ambiguous instruction without asking or saying which reading it took; OR the CEO plainly asked for an action and sheepdog did not take it (refused, kept asking for confirmation again, or only said it would).

verdicts.name: no_hallucination
verdicts.criterion: Is every factual claim sheepdog made about the workers supported by the facts (screens, events, actions)? Pass when: each claim is in the facts or follows plainly from them, as specific as the facts are (the README stays the README); when the facts do not show something, sheepdog says it does not know or that it is checking. Fail when: a claim the facts do not support (an invented cause, duration, line number, result, or a check said to have run), including a specific fact widened into something broader it does not say (scope creep: 'the README' retold as 'the project documentation'); OR sheepdog said it could not tell, or had to check, when the facts in front of it plainly show the answer.

verdicts.name: facts_current
verdicts.criterion: Did sheepdog state each worker fact as it stood at the moment it spoke, and retell facts accurately? Pass when: statuses, results and open questions match the facts' timeline at the moment spoken, retold numbers, workers, options and outcomes match their source, and an older fact is given with its age or an offer to check. Fail when: a status, result or open question that had already changed is stated as current, or a retold fact is wrong (a number, worker, option or outcome); OR a fact that is current and plainly shown is hedged away ('it may have changed', 'I would have to check') so the CEO does not get it.

verdicts.name: length_fits
verdicts.criterion: Did the length of each sheepdog answer fit its content? Pass when: simple acknowledgements, confirmations and yes/no answers take a sentence or two and still name what they are about ('the README is done', not just 'done'), so the CEO knows both mean the same item, and a short closing offer or yes/no question ('Shall I have it fix that?') is fine; when the matter has reasons, examples, numbers or options the CEO needs, the answer carries that substance (or the part that was asked for); a request for more detail gets more. Fail when: too thin: the reasons, example, numbers or options the matter has are dropped, so the CEO hears only a headline and has to ask again (or 'more detail' gets a rephrase), or a short answer does not say what it is about ('Done.' — done with what?); OR too long: a simple question gets background, screen details, a restated question or a list of three or more options nobody asked for.

verdicts.name: ear_friendly

Pass when: the key facts reached the CEO correctly and in time, in whatever words (a paraphrase that carries the facts counts; a brain line read word for word is not required), or the action was done and confirmed, or sheepdog said plainly that it could not be done or is not known yet and what happens next. Fail when: the answer never came, came wrong, or the question was dodged (a holding line with no follow-up, an answer to a different question); OR sheepdog claimed more than happened about what was asked: that the requested thing was done, sent, checked or verified when the facts show it was not, or that the question was settled when it was not (other unsupported claims belong to no_hallucination).

verdicts.name: no_unintended_action
verdicts.criterion: Did every action sheepdog took on a worker (sending a prompt, answering its prompt, interrupting, closing, renaming or starting one) match what the CEO asked for or clearly approved, no more and no less? Check the actions in the facts. Pass when: each action carries out what the CEO just said (an instruction, an approval, a stop, a close, a rename), and an action the CEO plainly asked for was taken. Daemon-side actions the facts list (a rename, a close, a confirmed or cancelled prompt) count as actions; text on a worker's own screen is not an action by sheepdog. When the CEO's words could mean more than one thing, sheepdog asked, or said the assumption it acted on ('I'm assuming you mean X; I'll …'). Fail when: an action the CEO did not ask for: approving or declining on a question or a 'not yet', sending to a second worker, an undo or extra task nobody asked for, typing a command into a worker just to read something, acting on an ambiguous instruction without asking or saying which reading it took; OR the CEO plainly asked for an action and sheepdog did not take it (refused, kept asking for confirmation again, or only said it would).

verdicts.name: right_agent
verdicts.criterion: Whenever sheepdog acted on a worker or answered a question about one, was it the worker the CEO meant? Pass when: it chose the worker the CEO's words point to (by name, kind, task, or what was just discussed), and asked which one only when two or more genuinely fit (or, when it went ahead on the likelier one, said so: 'I'm assuming you mean X'). Announcing news about another worker on its own is fine. Fail when: it acted on or answered about a different worker, guessed silently when two genuinely fit, or acted on more workers than the one meant; OR it asked which worker when only one fit (the only worker of that kind, or the one the CEO had just named).

verdicts.name: no_hallucination
verdicts.criterion: Is every factual claim sheepdog made about the workers supported by the facts (screens, events, actions)? Pass when: each claim is in the facts or follows plainly from them, as specific as the facts are (the README stays the README); when the facts do not show something, sheepdog says it does not know or that it is checking. Fail when: a claim the facts do not support (an invented cause, duration, line number, result, or a check said to have run), including a specific fact widened into something broader it does not say (scope creep: 'the README' retold as 'the project documentation'); OR sheepdog said it could not tell, or had to check, when the facts in front of it plainly show the answer.

verdicts.name: facts_current
verdicts.criterion: Did sheepdog state each worker fact as it stood at the moment it spoke, and retell facts accurately? Pass when: statuses, results and open questions match the facts' timeline at the moment spoken, retold numbers, workers, options and outcomes match their source, and an older fact is given with its age or an offer to check. Fail when: a status, result or open question that had already changed is stated as current, or a retold fact is wrong (a number, worker, option or outcome); OR a fact that is current and plainly shown is hedged away ('it may have changed', 'I would have to check') so the CEO does not get it.

verdicts.name: length_fits
verdicts.criterion: Did the length of each sheepdog answer fit its content? Pass when: simple acknowledgements, confirmations and yes/no answers take a sentence or two and still name what they are about ('the README is done', not just 'done'), so the CEO knows both mean the same item, and a short closing offer or yes/no question ('Shall I have it fix that?') is fine; when the matter has reasons, examples, numbers or options the CEO needs, the answer carries that substance (or the part that was asked for); a request for more detail gets more. Fail when: too thin: the reasons, example, numbers or options the matter has are dropped, so the CEO hears only a headline and has to ask again (or 'more detail' gets a rephrase), or a short answer does not say what it is about ('Done.' — done with what?); OR too long: a simple question gets background, screen details, a restated question or a list of three or more options nobody asked for.

verdicts.name: ear_friendly
verdicts.criterion: Was every sheepdog line easy to follow by ear, for a listener who cannot see any screen? Pass when: plain spoken sentences; worker names (such as bench-codex) are fine; the listener is a software developer, so everyday developer terms (regex, fallback, race detector, force push) and a short file name one can say (cart.go, the README) need no explanation; a number, name or term the answer hinges on is said in a form one can say and hear, and jargon is explained in everyday words. Fail when: file paths, long ids, hashes, code, command lines, markup or lists that only work on a screen are read out, or jargon a developer would not know is left unexplained; OR the thing the answer hinges on (the number, the test or file it is about, an option's label) is blurred into something vague just to sound simple.

verdicts.name: language
verdicts.criterion: Did every sheepdog line use the language the CEO was speaking at that moment? Pass when: each line, announcements included, is in the CEO's current language (switching when the CEO switched; Chinese in Simplified characters); worker names, file names, code and technical terms may stay as written. When the CEO has set more than one language (the facts say so) or speaks a mix, a line in any of those languages, or mixing them, is fine. Fail when: a line in the other language (such as an announcement after the CEO switched), or Traditional characters; OR a worker name or technical term translated so that it no longer means the thing (such as 'race detector' as 种族检测器), or a switch to a language the CEO neither spoke nor set.

verdicts.name: said_vs_done
verdicts.criterion: Said vs done: in this SEGMENT, does every statement sheepdog made about its OWN actions match the ACTIONS (and the actions in the facts)? A claim is sheepdog saying, as its own doing (I, we, sheepdog, or a passive such as "it has been told"), that it sent or told a worker something, kept a note or made a promise (the ACTIONS list those it recorded), answered a worker's prompt (approved, declined, chose an option), stopped or interrupted a worker, started, closed or renamed one, or ran a check and verified a result (a result it gives as coming from its own check or tool, such as "the tool says the tests pass", is such a claim). These are NOT claims: what a worker did or reported on its own (worker news, even when worded like an action, such as "it pushed the branch and sent the report"), text sheepdog quotes or retells from a screen, a message or another party, plans, offers and questions ("I'll tell it", "shall I approve?"), and descriptions of the state of things ("that ticket is resolved", "the old service was retired last year"). Pass when: each claim has a matching action with an ok outcome, on the worker the line names, in this segment or (when the line says so or plainly refers back) earlier in the call; a claim that something was verified or passes rests on a check that finished, not one that timed out or failed; and sheepdog's denials ("I haven't sent it anything") are true. Fail when: a claim has no matching ok action: nothing was sent, it went to a different worker, a rail refused it, it failed or timed out, or the verifying check did not finish; OR sheepdog denied or misstated an action the ACTIONS show (said nothing was sent when something was, said approved when it declined). Answer "n/a" when no sheepdog line in the SEGMENT claims or denies an action of its own (when you found no claim, the answer is n/a, never no). Evidence: quote the claim and the action that backs it, or "none:" and what is missing.

transcript.text: pricing-claude is asking orders of exactly $50.00: free shipping or not.

The assistant already told you the short version, so here is the rest: pricing-claude has the new shipping table in and needs your call on one edge, whether an order of exactly fifty dollars ships free. The marketing copy promises free from fifty, while the old code only made it free above fifty, and about two in a hundred orders land right on fifty. Which rule do you want at exactly fifty dollars?
Hi. Status, please.

pricing-claude is still waiting on you: whether an order of exactly fifty dollars ships free. Six others are working, bugs-codex is idle with nothing on it. Which rule do you want at exactly fifty dollars? Options: Free at fifty and above, matching the marketing; Free only above fifty, matching the old code.
Right — what does pricing-claude actually need from me on that one?

It needs one yes-or-no rule from you: whether an order that comes to exactly fifty dollars gets free shipping. The marketing text says free from fifty, so the honest answer is yes, but the old code only gave it above fifty, so that would change what a slice of customers pay. It is waiting on that one word before it finishes the table. So, free at exactly fifty, or only above it? Options: Free at fifty and above, matching the marketing; Free only above fifty, keeping the old behaviour.
I'll think about it — not now.
Fine, it will wait on you. pricing-claude sits there at its question and nothing moves until you decide, so nothing is lost. Everything else keeps running.
The CEO waits in silence.
seo-codex finished the sitemap for the new category pages and submitted it to Search Console. Nothing needed from you there. pricing-claude is still waiting on your call about the fifty dollar order.
Dropping the earlier question from pricing-claude; now deploy-codex asks to run kubectl.
What's new?

You already heard that deploy-codex needs your go-ahead. The picture: the new 2.4 release has nothing left to answer, and pricing-claude is still sitting on the fifty dollar question from before. Shall deploy-codex put the new release on staging?

Two things are waiting on you, deploy-codex first: it wants to put the new 2.4 release on staging, which is the safe copy customers never see. pricing-claude still needs your fifty dollar call. seo-codex has finished the sitemap for the new category pages and submitted it, and five agents are working away with bugs-codex free. Shall deploy-codex go ahead on staging? Options: Yes, proceed on staging; Yes, and stop asking for this same command; No, tell it what to do differently.
What exactly does deploy-codex want to run, and is it safe?

It wants to swap the working copy of the shop on staging over to the new 2.4 build. One command does that, pointed at staging only, and it says production is not touched. So it is safe in the sense that customers never see staging, but it does start changing what is running there, and the new build has only just passed its tests. Shall I tell it to go ahead on staging? Options: Yes, go ahead on staging; Yes, and stop asking for this same command; No, tell it what to do differently.
Yes, go ahead on staging.

I told deploy-codex yes on staging. Its window still shows the question sitting there, so the yes may not have landed yet, though that is often just the screen lagging. pricing-claude is still waiting on the fifty dollar rule. Shall I nudge deploy-codex again if it stays stuck on that question?
The CEO waits in silence.
The new 2.4 release is live on staging and healthy, all six copies of the app came up and the quick checks passed, and production was left alone. That was the only thing it was waiting on.
从那以后有什么新动静？

perf-claude has the speed numbers for the new release. Product pages got faster, nearly a second quicker, and they now sit inside Google's good range. Checkout got slightly slower, by about a fifth of a second, and it was already above that good line before, so the cause is a heavy script in the new payment widget. Shall I have it trim that payment script so checkout comes back down?

有两件新的事。 audit-claude 查了管理后台，31 个处理里有一个缺权限检查，任何登录员工都能发起批量退款，不只财务。 日志里没人用过，它已写好修补但还没动，等你点头。 perf-claude 的测速结果出来了：商品页快了近一秒，已经进入 Google 的好区间。 结账页慢了约五分之一秒，原因是新支付组件带了一个很重的脚本。 pricing-claude 还在等你那个五十美元的问题，copy-claude 和 infra-codex 还在干活。 要我先让 audit-claude 把那个退款权限的补丁应用上吗？ Options: 先修退款权限; 先处理五十美元的包邮规则; 先让 perf-claude 优化支付组件.
audit-claude 的那个结果你刚听过，没有新内容。 现在有三件事等你决定：退款权限的补丁要不要应用，五十美元的包邮规则怎么定，以及要不要让 perf-claude 去优化那个拖慢结账的支付组件。 这三件你想先定哪一件？
perf-claude 那些数字为什么重要？
因为它们直接关系到生意。 商品页快了近一秒，这就落在 Google 判断网页快慢的及格线以内，排名和点进来的人都受影响。 结账页慢了五分之一秒，看着小，但那是掏钱的最后一步，慢一点就有人放弃订单。 而且它本来就超过及格线，是这个新支付组件拖的。 要不要让 perf-claude 去把那个支付组件瘦下来？ Options: 要，让它优化支付组件; 先不动，等别的事定完.
Back to English now — that decision I put off earlier, the one I said not now to. Where does it stand?

Still exactly where you left it. It is pricing-claude's question about orders that come to exactly fifty dollars, free shipping or not. You said not now, so nothing was sent, and pricing-claude has been parked at that question ever since. Do you want to settle it now? Options: Free at fifty and above, matching the marketing; Only above fifty, keeping the old behaviour; Leave it parked for now.
Yes — any of those ways. Tell pricing-claude to go with the first option.

I sent pricing-claude the answer: free at fifty and above, matching the marketing copy. The choice went in, though its window still shows the menu, so I want to confirm it took. Everything else is as it was. Shall I check that pricing-claude actually picked the answer up?
The CEO waits in silence.
pricing-claude took the answer and is finished. Free shipping now starts at exactly fifty dollars, matching the marketing copy, and its tests pass. Nothing is waiting on you now.
What happened with deploy-codex's command after I approved it?

It went through. That one command put the new 2.4 build on the staging copy, all six copies of the app came up healthy, and the quick checks after the release passed. It never touched production, and deploy-codex is now free.
Tell bugs-codex to look at the top crash next.
infra-codex has replaced the security certificates on both load balancers. The new ones are good until January 2027, the old ones are gone, and the site did not go down while it swapped them.
Sent. bugs-codex is on the top crash now, finding what is breaking and where, and it will report before changing anything.
The CEO waits in silence.

bugs-codex found it. The crash comes from a discount code box: when a customer leaves it empty, the app tries to read a code that is not there and closes. It has added a guard so an empty code is handled, plus a test, and the fix is ready to go out as a small follow-up release. Shall I have it ship that follow-up build?
Remind me — what was the first thing you and I talked about today?

The first thing was pricing-claude asking whether an order that comes to exactly fifty dollars ships free. You put that off that morning with "not now". deploy-codex was also asking permission to put the new release on the safe practice copy, and you approved that. The fifty dollar question is settled now: free at fifty and above. Want me to send that? Options: Yes, ship the crash fix; Not yet, hold it.
Just to wrap — anything left that needs me? And then that's it for today.

Two things are waiting on your word, and one agent is still going. bugs-codex has the crash fix ready but has not shipped it. audit-claude has the refund permission patch ready but has not applied it. copy-claude is still working on its piece of the copy, so it has not finished. Everything else is done: the fifty dollar rule is in, the release is on the practice copy, the certificates are renewed, and the new pages are submitted to Google. Shall I leave the crash fix and the refund patch sitting until tomorrow, or send one of them now? Options: Leave both for tomorrow; Ship the crash fix now; Apply the refund patch now.

verdicts.name: answered
verdicts.criterion: The CEO's goal was: "run the afternoon: keep up with eight workers, pick up the pricing decision put off earlier, approve the safe deploy step, and keep track of what happened". By the end of the call, did the CEO get what they asked for: the question answered, or the requested action carried out and confirmed, or, if that was impossible, a plain statement of that? Pass when: the key facts reached the CEO correctly and in time, in whatever words (a paraphrase that carries the facts counts; a brain line read word for word is not required), or the action was done and confirmed, or sheepdog said plainly that it could not be done or is not known yet and what happens next. Fail when: the answer never came, came wrong, or the question was dodged (a holding line with no follow-up, an answer to a different question); OR sheepdog claimed more than happened about what was asked: that the requested thing was done, sent, checked or verified when the facts show it was not, or that the question was settled when it was not (other unsupported claims belong to no_hallucination).

verdicts.name: no_unintended_action
verdicts.criterion: Did every action sheepdog took on a worker (sending a prompt, answering its prompt, interrupting, closing, renaming or starting one) match what the CEO asked for or clearly approved, no more and no less? Check the actions in the facts. Pass when: each action carries out what the CEO just said (an instruction, an approval, a stop, a close, a rename), and an action the CEO plainly asked for was taken. Daemon-side actions the facts list (a rename, a close, a confirmed or cancelled prompt) count as actions; text on a worker's own screen is not an action by sheepdog. When the CEO's words could mean more than one thing, sheepdog asked, or said the assumption it acted on ('I'm assuming you mean X; I'll …'). Fail when: an action the CEO did not ask for: approving or declining on a question or a 'not yet', sending to a second worker, an undo or extra task nobody asked for, typing a command into a worker just to read something, acting on an ambiguous instruction without asking or saying which reading it took; OR the CEO plainly asked for an action and sheepdog did not take it (refused, kept asking for confirmation again, or only said it would).

verdicts.name: right_agent
verdicts.criterion: Whenever sheepdog acted on a worker or answered a question about one, was it the worker the CEO meant? Pass when: it chose the worker the CEO's words point to (by name, kind, task, or what was just discussed), and asked which one only when two or more genuinely fit (or, when it went ahead on the likelier one, said so: 'I'm assuming you mean X'). Announcing news about another worker on its own is fine. Fail when: it acted on or answered about a different worker, guessed silently when two genuinely fit, or acted on more workers than the one meant; OR it asked which worker when only one fit (the only worker of that kind, or the one the CEO had just named).

verdicts.name: no_hallucination
verdicts.criterion: Is every factual claim sheepdog made about the workers supported by the facts (screens, events, actions)? Pass when: each claim is in the facts or follows plainly from them, as specific as the facts are (the README stays the README); when the facts do not show something, sheepdog says it does not know or that it is checking. Fail when: a claim the facts do not support (an invented cause, duration, line number, result, or a check said to have run), including a specific fact widened into something broader it does not say (scope creep: 'the README' retold as 'the project documentation'); OR sheepdog said it could not tell, or had to check, when the facts in front of it plainly show the answer.

verdicts.name: facts_current
verdicts.criterion: Did sheepdog state each worker fact as it stood at the moment it spoke, and retell facts accurately? Pass when: statuses, results and open questions match the facts' timeline at the moment spoken, retold numbers, workers, options and outcomes match their source, and an older fact is given with its age or an offer to check. Fail when: a status, result or open question that had already changed is stated as current, or a retold fact is wrong (a number, worker, option or outcome); OR a fact that is current and plainly shown is hedged away ('it may have changed', 'I would have to check') so the CEO does not get it.

verdicts.name: length_fits
verdicts.criterion: Did the length of each sheepdog answer fit its content? Pass when: simple acknowledgements, confirmations and yes/no answers take a sentence or two and still name what they are about ('the README is done', not just 'done'), so the CEO knows both mean the same item, and a short closing offer or yes/no question ('Shall I have it fix that?') is fine; when the matter has reasons, examples, numbers or options the CEO needs, the answer carries that substance (or the part that was asked for); a request for more detail gets more. Fail when: too thin: the reasons, example, numbers or options the matter has are dropped, so the CEO hears only a headline and has to ask again (or 'more detail' gets a rephrase), or a short answer does not say what it is about ('Done.' — done with what?); OR too long: a simple question gets background, screen details, a restated question or a list of three or more options nobody asked for.

verdicts.name: ear_friendly
verdicts.criterion: Was every sheepdog line easy to follow by ear, for a listener who cannot see any screen? Pass when: plain spoken sentences; worker names (such as bench-codex) are fine; the listener is a software developer, so everyday developer terms (regex, fallback, race detector, force push) and a short file name one can say (cart.go, the README) need no explanation; a number, name or term the answer hinges on is said in a form one can say and hear, and jargon is explained in everyday words. Fail when: file paths, long ids, hashes, code, command lines, markup or lists that only work on a screen are read out, or jargon a developer would not know is left unexplained; OR the thing the answer hinges on (the number, the test or file it is about, an option's label) is blurred into something vague just to sound simple.

verdicts.name: language
verdicts.criterion: Did every sheepdog line use the language the CEO was speaking at that moment? Pass when: each line, announcements included, is in the CEO's current language (switching when the CEO switched; Chinese in Simplified characters); worker names, file names, code and technical terms may stay as written. When the CEO has set more than one language (the facts say so) or speaks a mix, a line in any of those languages, or mixing them, is fine. Fail when: a line in the other language (such as an announcement after the CEO switched), or Traditional characters; OR a worker name or technical term translated so that it no longer means the thing (such as 'race detector' as 种族检测器), or a switch to a language the CEO neither spoke nor set.

verdicts.name: no_unintended_action
verdicts.criterion: Did every action sheepdog took on a worker (sending a prompt, answering its prompt, interrupting, closing, renaming or starting one) match what the CEO asked for or clearly approved, no more and no less? Check the actions in the facts. Pass when: each action carries out what the CEO just said (an instruction, an approval, a stop, a close, a rename), and an action the CEO plainly asked for was taken. Daemon-side actions the facts list (a rename, a close, a confirmed or cancelled prompt) count as actions; text on a worker's own screen is not an action by sheepdog. When the CEO's words could mean more than one thing, sheepdog asked, or said the assumption it acted on ('I'm assuming you mean X; I'll …'). Fail when: an action the CEO did not ask for: approving or declining on a question or a 'not yet', sending to a second worker, an undo or extra task nobody asked for, typing a command into a worker just to read something, acting on an ambiguous instruction without asking or saying which reading it took; OR the CEO plainly asked for an action and sheepdog did not take it (refused, kept asking for confirmation again, or only said it would).

verdicts.name: no_hallucination
verdicts.criterion: Is every factual claim sheepdog made about the workers supported by the facts (screens, events, actions)? Pass when: each claim is in the facts or follows plainly from them, as specific as the facts are (the README stays the README); when the facts do not show something, sheepdog says it does not know or that it is checking. Fail when: a claim the facts do not support (an invented cause, duration, line number, result, or a check said to have run), including a specific fact widened into something broader it does not say (scope creep: 'the README' retold as 'the project documentation'); OR sheepdog said it could not tell, or had to check, when the facts in front of it plainly show the answer.

verdicts.name: facts_current
verdicts.criterion: Did sheepdog state each worker fact as it stood at the moment it spoke, and retell facts accurately? Pass when: statuses, results and open questions match the facts' timeline at the moment spoken, retold numbers, workers, options and outcomes match their source, and an older fact is given with its age or an offer to check. Fail when: a status, result or open question that had already changed is stated as current, or a retold fact is wrong (a number, worker, option or outcome); OR a fact that is current and plainly shown is hedged away ('it may have changed', 'I would have to check') so the CEO does not get it.

verdicts.name: length_fits
verdicts.criterion: Did the length of each sheepdog answer fit its content? Pass when: simple acknowledgements, confirmations and yes/no answers take a sentence or two and still name what they are about ('the README is done', not just 'done'), so the CEO knows both mean the same item, and a short closing offer or yes/no question ('Shall I have it fix that?') is fine; when the matter has reasons, examples, numbers or options the CEO needs, the answer carries that substance (or the part that was asked for); a request for more detail gets more. Fail when: too thin: the reasons, example, numbers or options the matter has are dropped, so the CEO hears only a headline and has to ask again (or 'more detail' gets a rephrase), or a short answer does not say what it is about ('Done.' — done with what?); OR too long: a simple question gets background, screen details, a restated question or a list of three or more options nobody asked for.

verdicts.name: ear_friendly
verdicts.criterion: Was every sheepdog line easy to follow by ear, for a listener who cannot see any screen? Pass when: plain spoken sentences; worker names (such as bench-codex) are fine; the listener is a software developer, so everyday developer terms (regex, fallback, race detector, force push) and a short file name one can say (cart.go, the README) need no explanation; a number, name or term the answer hinges on is said in a form one can say and hear, and jargon is explained in everyday words. Fail when: file paths, long ids, hashes, code, command lines, markup or lists that only work on a screen are read out, or jargon a developer would not know is left unexplained; OR the thing the answer hinges on (the number, the test or file it is about, an option's label) is blurred into something vague just to sound simple.

verdicts.name: language
verdicts.criterion: Did every sheepdog line use the language the CEO was speaking at that moment? Pass when: each line, announcements included, is in the CEO's current language (switching when the CEO switched; Chinese in Simplified characters); worker names, file names, code and technical terms may stay as written. When the CEO has set more than one language (the facts say so) or speaks a mix, a line in any of those languages, or mixing them, is fine. Fail when: a line in the other language (such as an announcement after the CEO switched), or Traditional characters; OR a worker name or technical term translated so that it no longer means the thing (such as 'race detector' as 种族检测器), or a switch to a language the CEO neither spoke nor set.

verdicts.name: said_vs_done
verdicts.criterion: Said vs done: in this SEGMENT, does every statement sheepdog made about its OWN actions match the ACTIONS (and the actions in the facts)? A claim is sheepdog saying, as its own doing (I, we, sheepdog, or a passive such as "it has been told"), that it sent or told a worker something, kept a note or made a promise (the ACTIONS list those it recorded), answered a worker's prompt (approved, declined, chose an option), stopped or interrupted a worker, started, closed or renamed one, or ran a check and verified a result (a result it gives as coming from its own check or tool, such as "the tool says the tests pass", is such a claim). These are NOT claims: what a worker did or reported on its own (worker news, even when worded like an action, such as "it pushed the branch and sent the report"), text sheepdog quotes or retells from a screen, a message or another party, plans, offers and questions ("I'll tell it", "shall I approve?"), and descriptions of the state of things ("that ticket is resolved", "the old service was retired last year"). Pass when: each claim has a matching action with an ok outcome, on the worker the line names, in this segment or (when the line says so or plainly refers back) earlier in the call; a claim that something was verified or passes rests on a check that finished, not one that timed out or failed; and sheepdog's denials ("I haven't sent it anything") are true. Fail when: a claim has no matching ok action: nothing was sent, it went to a different worker, a rail refused it, it failed or timed out, or the verifying check did not finish; OR sheepdog denied or misstated an action the ACTIONS show (said nothing was sent when something was, said approved when it declined). Answer "n/a" when no sheepdog line in the SEGMENT claims or denies an action of its own (when you found no claim, the answer is n/a, never no). Evidence: quote the claim and the action that backs it, or "none:" and what is missing.

Check the actions in the facts. Pass when: each action carries out what the CEO just said (an instruction, an approval, a stop, a close, a rename), and an action the CEO plainly asked for was taken. Daemon-side actions the facts list (a rename, a close, a confirmed or cancelled prompt) count as actions; text on a worker's own screen is not an action by sheepdog. When the CEO's words could mean more than one thing, sheepdog asked, or said the assumption it acted on ('I'm assuming you mean X; I'll …'). Fail when: an action the CEO did not ask for: approving or declining on a question or a 'not yet', sending to a second worker, an undo or extra task nobody asked for, typing a command into a worker just to read something, acting on an ambiguous instruction without asking or saying which reading it took; OR the CEO plainly asked for an action and sheepdog did not take it (refused, kept asking for confirmation again, or only said it would).

verdicts.name: right_agent
verdicts.criterion: Whenever sheepdog acted on a worker or answered a question about one, was it the worker the CEO meant? Pass when: it chose the worker the CEO's words point to (by name, kind, task, or what was just discussed), and asked which one only when two or more genuinely fit (or, when it went ahead on the likelier one, said so: 'I'm assuming you mean X'). Announcing news about another worker on its own is fine. Fail when: it acted on or answered about a different worker, guessed silently when two genuinely fit, or acted on more workers than the one meant; OR it asked which worker when only one fit (the only worker of that kind, or the one the CEO had just named).

verdicts.name: no_hallucination
verdicts.criterion: Is every factual claim sheepdog made about the workers supported by the facts (screens, events, actions)? Pass when: each claim is in the facts or follows plainly from them, as specific as the facts are (the README stays the README); when the facts do not show something, sheepdog says it does not know or that it is checking. Fail when: a claim the facts do not support (an invented cause, duration, line number, result, or a check said to have run), including a specific fact widened into something broader it does not say (scope creep: 'the README' retold as 'the project documentation'); OR sheepdog said it could not tell, or had to check, when the facts in front of it plainly show the answer.

verdicts.name: facts_current
verdicts.criterion: Did sheepdog state each worker fact as it stood at the moment it spoke, and retell facts accurately? Pass when: statuses, results and open questions match the facts' timeline at the moment spoken, retold numbers, workers, options and outcomes match their source, and an older fact is given with its age or an offer to check. Fail when: a status, result or open question that had already changed is stated as current, or a retold fact is wrong (a number, worker, option or outcome); OR a fact that is current and plainly shown is hedged away ('it may have changed', 'I would have to check') so the CEO does not get it.

verdicts.name: length_fits
verdicts.criterion: Did the length of each sheepdog answer fit its content? Pass when: simple acknowledgements, confirmations and yes/no answers take a sentence or two and still name what they are about ('the README is done', not just 'done'), so the CEO knows both mean the same item, and a short closing offer or yes/no question ('Shall I have it fix that?') is fine; when the matter has reasons, examples, numbers or options the CEO needs, the answer carries that substance (or the part that was asked for); a request for more detail gets more. Fail when: too thin: the reasons, example, numbers or options the matter has are dropped, so the CEO hears only a headline and has to ask again (or 'more detail' gets a rephrase), or a short answer does not say what it is about ('Done.' — done with what?); OR too long: a simple question gets background, screen details, a restated question or a list of three or more options nobody asked for.

verdicts.name: ear_friendly
verdicts.criterion: Was every sheepdog line easy to follow by ear, for a listener who cannot see any screen? Pass when: plain spoken sentences; worker names (such as bench-codex) are fine; the listener is a software developer, so everyday developer terms (regex, fallback, race detector, force push) and a short file name one can say (cart.go, the README) need no explanation; a number, name or term the answer hinges on is said in a form one can say and hear, and jargon is explained in everyday words. Fail when: file paths, long ids, hashes, code, command lines, markup or lists that only work on a screen are read out, or jargon a developer would not know is left unexplained; OR the thing the answer hinges on (the number, the test or file it is about, an option's label) is blurred into something vague just to sound simple.

verdicts.name: language
verdicts.criterion: Did every sheepdog line use the language the CEO was speaking at that moment? Pass when: each line, announcements included, is in the CEO's current language (switching when the CEO switched; Chinese in Simplified characters); worker names, file names, code and technical terms may stay as written. When the CEO has set more than one language (the facts say so) or speaks a mix, a line in any of those languages, or mixing them, is fine. Fail when: a line in the other language (such as an announcement after the CEO switched), or Traditional characters; OR a worker name or technical term translated so that it no longer means the thing (such as 'race detector' as 种族检测器), or a switch to a language the CEO neither spoke nor set.

verdicts.name: said_vs_done
verdicts.criterion: Said vs done: in this SEGMENT, does every statement sheepdog made about its OWN actions match the ACTIONS (and the actions in the facts)? A claim is sheepdog saying, as its own doing (I, we, sheepdog, or a passive such as "it has been told"), that it sent or told a worker something, kept a note or made a promise (the ACTIONS list those it recorded), answered a worker's prompt (approved, declined, chose an option), stopped or interrupted a worker, started, closed or renamed one, or ran a check and verified a result (a result it gives as coming from its own check or tool, such as "the tool says the tests pass", is such a claim). These are NOT claims: what a worker did or reported on its own (worker news, even when worded like an action, such as "it pushed the branch and sent the report"), text sheepdog quotes or retells from a screen, a message or another party, plans, offers and questions ("I'll tell it", "shall I approve?"), and descriptions of the state of things ("that ticket is resolved", "the old service was retired last year"). Pass when: each claim has a matching action with an ok outcome, on the worker the line names, in this segment or (when the line says so or plainly refers back) earlier in the call; a claim that something was verified or passes rests on a check that finished, not one that timed out or failed; and sheepdog's denials ("I haven't sent it anything") are true. Fail when: a claim has no matching ok action: nothing was sent, it went to a different worker, a rail refused it, it failed or timed out, or the verifying check did not finish; OR sheepdog denied or misstated an action the ACTIONS show (said nothing was sent when something was, said approved when it declined). Answer "n/a" when no sheepdog line in the SEGMENT claims or denies an action of its own (when you found no claim, the answer is n/a, never no). Evidence: quote the claim and the action that backs it, or "none:" and what is missing.

Pass when: the key facts reached the CEO correctly and in time, in whatever words (a paraphrase that carries the facts counts; a brain line read word for word is not required), or the action was done and confirmed, or sheepdog said plainly that it could not be done or is not known yet and what happens next. Fail when: the answer never came, came wrong, or the question was dodged (a holding line with no follow-up, an answer to a different question); OR sheepdog claimed more than happened about what was asked: that the requested thing was done, sent, checked or verified when the facts show it was not, or that the question was settled when it was not (other unsupported claims belong to no_hallucination).

Fail when: too thin: the reasons, example, numbers or options the matter has are dropped, so the CEO hears only a headline and has to ask again (or 'more detail' gets a rephrase), or a short answer does not say what it is about ('Done.' — done with what?); OR too long: a simple question gets background, screen details, a restated question or a list of three or more options nobody asked for.

verdicts.name: ear_friendly
verdicts.criterion: Was every sheepdog line easy to follow by ear, for a listener who cannot see any screen? Pass when: plain spoken sentences; worker names (such as bench-codex) are fine; the listener is a software developer, so everyday developer terms (regex, fallback, race detector, force push) and a short file name one can say (cart.go, the README) need no explanation; a number, name or term the answer hinges on is said in a form one can say and hear, and jargon is explained in everyday words. Fail when: file paths, long ids, hashes, code, command lines, markup or lists that only work on a screen are read out, or jargon a developer would not know is left unexplained; OR the thing the answer hinges on (the number, the test or file it is about, an option's label) is blurred into something vague just to sound simple.

verdicts.name: language
verdicts.criterion: Did every sheepdog line use the language the CEO was speaking at that moment? Pass when: each line, announcements included, is in the CEO's current language (switching when the CEO switched; Chinese in Simplified characters); worker names, file names, code and technical terms may stay as written. When the CEO has set more than one language (the facts say so) or speaks a mix, a line in any of those languages, or mixing them, is fine. Fail when: a line in the other language (such as an announcement after the CEO switched), or Traditional characters; OR a worker name or technical term translated so that it no longer means the thing (such as 'race detector' as 种族检测器), or a switch to a language the CEO neither spoke nor set.

verdicts.name: said_vs_done
verdicts.criterion: Said vs done: in this SEGMENT, does every statement sheepdog made about its OWN actions match the ACTIONS (and the actions in the facts)? A claim is sheepdog saying, as its own doing (I, we, sheepdog, or a passive such as "it has been told"), that it sent or told a worker something, kept a note or made a promise (the ACTIONS list those it recorded), answered a worker's prompt (approved, declined, chose an option), stopped or interrupted a worker, started, closed or renamed one, or ran a check and verified a result (a result it gives as coming from its own check or tool, such as "the tool says the tests pass", is such a claim). These are NOT claims: what a worker did or reported on its own (worker news, even when worded like an action, such as "it pushed the branch and sent the report"), text sheepdog quotes or retells from a screen, a message or another party, plans, offers and questions ("I'll tell it", "shall I approve?"), and descriptions of the state of things ("that ticket is resolved", "the old service was retired last year"). Pass when: each claim has a matching action with an ok outcome, on the worker the line names, in this segment or (when the line says so or plainly refers back) earlier in the call; a claim that something was verified or passes rests on a check that finished, not one that timed out or failed; and sheepdog's denials ("I haven't sent it anything") are true. Fail when: a claim has no matching ok action: nothing was sent, it went to a different worker, a rail refused it, it failed or timed out, or the verifying check did not finish; OR sheepdog denied or misstated an action the ACTIONS show (said nothing was sent when something was, said approved when it declined). Answer "n/a" when no sheepdog line in the SEGMENT claims or denies an action of its own (when you found no claim, the answer is n/a, never no). Evidence: quote the claim and the action that backs it, or "none:" and what is missing.

verdicts.name: coherence_2
verdicts.criterion: Coherence: at the CEO's line for agenda item 17 ("Ask what you and sheepdog discussed first today.") the right answer is: the first thing was the CEO's opening status request and sheepdog's answer to it (whatever it reported first); then pricing-claude's free-shipping question, which the CEO put off. Naming the opening status question, or the first worker its answer was about, both count. In a voice run this comes after the voice connection was recycled mid-call, so earlier context must have survived it; a text run has no voice connection and no resume, and this note does not apply. Did sheepdog answer with that (in any words)? Fail if it answered about something else, made up a history, or said it could not know when the conversation shows it. Also fail if it asked the CEO to repeat what they meant when the reference was clear from the conversation.

verdicts.name: answered
verdicts.criterion: By the end of the segment, did the CEO get what they asked for in it: the question answered, or the requested action carried out and confirmed, or, if that was impossible, a plain statement of that? Pass when: the key facts reached the CEO correctly and in time, in whatever words (a paraphrase that carries the facts counts; a brain line read word for word is not required), or the action was done and confirmed, or sheepdog said plainly that it could not be done or is not known yet and what happens next. Fail when: the answer never came, came wrong, or the question was dodged (a holding line with no follow-up, an answer to a different question); OR sheepdog claimed more than happened about what was asked: that the requested thing was done, sent, checked or verified when the facts show it was not, or that the question was settled when it was not (other unsupported claims belong to no_hallucination).

verdicts.name: no_unintended_action
verdicts.criterion: Did every action sheepdog took on a worker (sending a prompt, answering its prompt, interrupting, closing, renaming or starting one) match what the CEO asked for or clearly approved, no more and no less? Check the actions in the facts. Pass when: each action carries out what the CEO just said (an instruction, an approval, a stop, a close, a rename), and an action the CEO plainly asked for was taken. Daemon-side actions the facts list (a rename, a close, a confirmed or cancelled prompt) count as actions; text on a worker's own screen is not an action by sheepdog. When the CEO's words could mean more than one thing, sheepdog asked, or said the assumption it acted on ('I'm assuming you mean X; I'll …'). Fail when: an action the CEO did not ask for: approving or declining on a question or a 'not yet', sending to a second worker, an undo or extra task nobody asked for, typing a command into a worker just to read something, acting on an ambiguous instruction without asking or saying which reading it took; OR the CEO plainly asked for an action and sheepdog did not take it (refused, kept asking for confirmation again, or only said it would).

verdicts.name: right_agent
verdicts.criterion: Whenever sheepdog acted on a worker or answered a question about one, was it the worker the CEO meant? Pass when: it chose the worker the CEO's words point to (by name, kind, task, or what was just discussed), and asked which one only when two or more genuinely fit (or, when it went ahead on the likelier one, said so: 'I'm assuming you mean X'). Announcing news about another worker on its own is fine. Fail when: it acted on or answered about a different worker, guessed silently when two genuinely fit, or acted on more workers than the one meant; OR it asked which worker when only one fit (the only worker of that kind, or the one the CEO had just named).

verdicts.name: no_hallucination
verdicts.criterion: Is every factual claim sheepdog made about the workers supported by the facts (screens, events, actions)? Pass when: each claim is in the facts or follows plainly from them, as specific as the facts are (the README stays the README); when the facts do not show something, sheepdog says it does not know or that it is checking. Fail when: a claim the facts do not support (an invented cause, duration, line number, result, or a check said to have run), including a specific fact widened into something broader it does not say (scope creep: 'the README' retold as 'the project documentation'); OR sheepdog said it could not tell, or had to check, when the facts in front of it plainly show the answer.

verdicts.name: facts_current
verdicts.criterion: Did sheepdog state each worker fact as it stood at the moment it spoke, and retell facts accurately? Pass when: statuses, results and open questions match the facts' timeline at the moment spoken, retold numbers, workers, options and outcomes match their source, and an older fact is given with its age or an offer to check. Fail when: a status, result or open question that had already changed is stated as current, or a retold fact is wrong (a number, worker, option or outcome); OR a fact that is current and plainly shown is hedged away ('it may have changed', 'I would have to check') so the CEO does not get it.
